items.name: Artificial Intelligence
items.explanation: AI teaches computers to think, learn, and make decisions like humans

items.name: Machine Learning
items.explanation: ML lets computers learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task

items.name: Neural Networks
items.explanation: Neural networks are inspired by the brain and learn to recognize patterns in data

items.name: Deep Learning
items.explanation: Deep learning stacks many neural network layers to solve complex AI problems

items.name: Computer Vision
items.explanation: Computer vision lets machines see and understand images and video like humans do

items.name: NLP
items.explanation: Natural Language Processing helps computers read, understand, and generate human language

items.name: Reinforcement Learning
items.explanation: RL trains AI by rewarding good decisions — like teaching a dog new tricks with treats

items.name: Generative AI
items.explanation: Generative AI creates new content: text, images, audio, code, and video from scratch

items.name: Transfer Learning
items.explanation: Transfer learning reuses knowledge from one AI task to speed up solving another

items.name: AI Agents
items.explanation: AI agents can reason, plan, and take actions autonomously to complete complex tasks

items.name: Large Language Model
items.explanation: LLMs are AI trained on massive text data to understand and generate human language

items.name: Transformer
items.explanation: The Transformer architecture revolutionized AI with powerful self-attention mechanisms

items.name: Tokens
items.explanation: Tokens are the smallest text units LLMs process — roughly 0.75 words per token

items.name: Context Window
items.explanation: The context window is how much text an LLM can read and remember in one conversation

items.name: Prompt Engineering
items.explanation: Prompt engineering is crafting inputs to reliably get the best outputs from LLMs

items.name: Fine-tuning
items.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained LLM to a specific domain, task, or writing style

items.name: Embeddings
items.explanation: Embeddings are numerical vectors that capture the meaning of text for AI search and retrieval

items.name: Hallucination
items.explanation: LLM hallucination is when the model generates confident but factually incorrect answers

items.name: Temperature
items.explanation: Temperature controls how creative or random an LLM's output is — higher means more creative

items.name: System Prompt
items.explanation: A system prompt sets the AI assistant's role, persona, rules, and constraints upfront

items.name: RAG
items.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation combines search with LLMs to give accurate, grounded answers

items.name: Vector Database
items.explanation: Vector databases store embeddings and enable lightning-fast semantic similarity search

items.name: Chunking
items.explanation: Chunking splits documents into smaller pieces for efficient storage and relevant retrieval

items.name: Semantic Search
items.explanation: Semantic search finds results by meaning, not just keyword matching — much smarter

items.name: Re-ranking
items.explanation: Re-ranking re-orders retrieved results to improve relevance before passing them to the LLM

items.name: Knowledge Base
items.explanation: A knowledge base is your collection of documents that RAG searches to answer questions

items.name: Document Loader
items.explanation: Document loaders parse PDFs, web pages, and files into clean text for RAG pipelines

items.name: Query Expansion
items.explanation: Query expansion rewrites user questions multiple ways to improve search recall and coverage

items.name: Hybrid Search
items.explanation: Hybrid search combines keyword and semantic search for better, more reliable results

items.name: Context Window RAG
items.explanation: RAG stuffs retrieved documents into the LLM's context so it can answer with real knowledge

items.name: SQL
items.explanation: SQL is the standard language for querying and managing structured relational databases

items.name: NoSQL
items.explanation: NoSQL databases store unstructured or semi-structured data with flexible, scalable schemas

items.name: PostgreSQL
items.explanation: PostgreSQL is a powerful open-source relational database used by millions of applications

items.name: MongoDB
items.explanation: MongoDB stores data as JSON documents — great for flexible, rapidly changing data structures

items.name: Redis
items.explanation: Redis is an in-memory database used for caching, sessions, and real-time applications

items.name: Vector DB
items.explanation: Vector databases like Pinecone and Chroma store AI embeddings for fast similarity search

items.name: ACID
items.explanation: ACID ensures database transactions are Atomic, Consistent, Isolated, and Durable

items.name: Indexing
items.explanation: Database indexes dramatically speed up queries by creating shortcuts to find data fast

items.name: Graph Database
items.explanation: Graph databases like Neo4j model and query complex relationships between data points

items.name: Sharding
items.explanation: Sharding splits a database across multiple servers to handle massive scale and traffic

items.name: MCP
items.explanation: Model Context Protocol is an open standard connecting AI models to external tools and data

items.name: MCP Server
items.explanation: An MCP server exposes tools, resources, and prompts that any compatible AI client can use

items.name: MCP Client
items.explanation: MCP clients like Claude Desktop connect to servers to access their capabilities and data

items.name: Tools
items.explanation: MCP Tools let AI models execute functions like file operations, API calls, and web searches

items.name: Resources
items.explanation: MCP Resources expose data sources like files, databases, and APIs to AI models

items.name: Prompts
items.explanation: MCP Prompts are reusable prompt templates that standardize AI model behavior across apps

items.name: Sampling
items.explanation: MCP Sampling lets servers request LLM completions through the connected client

items.name: Transport
items.explanation: MCP supports stdio and HTTP with SSE transports for client-server communication

items.name: Claude Desktop
items.explanation: Claude Desktop natively supports MCP, letting you connect local and remote MCP servers

items.name: MCP SDK
items.explanation: The official MCP SDK lets developers build servers and clients in Python and TypeScript
